la:noun:proelium.html:
proelĭum (prael-), ii, n.
etym. dub.; perh. for provilium, pro-dvilium; cf. duellum (bellum)
,
a battle, combat (class.; syn.: pugna, dimicatio).
Lit.: induperatores pugnare ac proelia obire,: non proeliis, neque acie bellum gerere,: exitus proeliorum,: proelium facere,to engage,: inire,: committere cum aliquo,: redintegrare,: restituere,: conficere,: miscere,proelio dimicare cum hoste,: proeliis decertare,: proelium sumere,to join battle, engage,: singulare,single combat,: Punica passi proelia,the wars with Carthage,.—
Transf.
Of animals (poet.): proelia dant cervi,: (taurorum),; cf. ; .—
Of inanimate subjects (poet.): ventorum proelia,.—
A warrior: Colchis flagrantes adamantina sub juga tauros Egit et armigera proelia sevit humo, (4, 10), 10: trepidum si Martis operti agricolam infandis condentem proelia sulcis expediam,.—
Trop.
Contest, strife (class.): proelia te meā causā sustinere,: committere proelia voce,; .—Humorously, of a struggle with food and drink: in eo uterque proelio potabimus,: sed quid cessamus proelium committere?.—
In mal. part., : veneris,.

senses: alternative form of proelior (“to fight in battle”)
la:verb:proelio.html:
proelĭo, āre, 1, v. a. (ante-class.; collat. form of proelior): mortales inter sese pugnant, proeliant, Enn. ap. (Trag. v. 26 Vahl.); cf. P.—
Impers. pass.: proeliatum est,.

la:verb:proelior.html:
proelĭor (prael-), ātus, 1,
v. dep. n. [proelium], to join battle, to engage in battle, fight (class.).
Lit.: legiones in ipsis fluminis ripis proeliabantur,: pedibus,: ad Syracusas,: ita proelians interficitur,: fortissime proeliando,: apes inter se et cum alteris quasi cum exteris gentibus proeliantur,; cf. ; ; : bella Domini, et saep.—
Transf.
In mal. part.: ex animo proeliabor,.—
In gen., to contend,fight with words: vehementer proeliatus sum,.

la:adj:proeliaris.gloss: of or pertaining to a battle
senses: of or pertaining to a battle

proelĭāris (prael-) and proelĭā-lis, e, adj.
proelium
,
